thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated gateway 502/504s and increased timeouts detected across public-api cluster starting ~04:18 UTC. Aggregate 5xx ~6% (baseline 0.6%). Paging oncall. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/gw-5xx-uptick
leah_oncall: ACKed. pulling traces and recent deploys. Noticed a batch compaction job finished at 04:15.
rajan_sre: digging into kv-prefix metrics — shard 22 shows a sharp eviction spike and a sudden jump in repair_retries. Prefetch queue depth went from 10 to 120. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/kvcache?shard=22&from=04:00
emma_eng: backend logs include repeated `kv: inconsistent-prefix-digest` errors plus `store: prefetch retry limit reached` around 04:16. Example: ```
2026-03-15T04:16:02Z store ERROR shard=22 event="inconsistent-prefix-digest" prefix=/models/alpha id=0x9f3a
2026-03-15T04:16:03Z prefetch WARN shard=22 retries=4 prefix=/models/alpha latency=950ms
```
ops_maya: hypothesis: compaction job might have produced stale digests for a subset of prefixes -> clients detect mismatch -> evictions + synchronous prefetches -> backend saturation -> gateway timeouts. Could also be a failed mirror sync.
leah_oncall: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) flip `gateway.cache_circuit=opened` for problematic routes to short-circuit cache reads 2) throttle prefetch workers on shard 20-24 3) isolate shard 22 from read replicas to stop high-ttl rehydration 4) notify support. Which command toggles circuit?
rajan_sre: we use cfgctl: `cfgctl set proxy.gateway.cache_circuit open --scope route=/v1/*` — I'll apply to prod with 5-min ttl. Also reduce prefetch workers: `kvctl set-workers --shards 20-24 --workers 2`.
infra_bot: change submitted: id=chg-9902 by rajan_sre; cache_circuit=opened for /v1/*; status=applied to 40% of hosts
emma_eng: applying worker throttle now. Running `kvctl`... done. Prefetch workers down to 2 for 20-24.
leah_oncall: after circuit open + worker throttle, 5xx fell to 2.1% at 04:25. Still seeing timeouts for some customers on dedicated infra.
cs_paul: FYI support: 3 customers reported 502s (acct A12, B34, C56). Sending short note now.
ops_maya: next: mark shard 22 read-only to avoid writes causing more digest churn, and run a quick digest-recompute for that shard. Command: `kvadmin set-shard-mode 22 readonly --reason "digest-drift-2026-03-15"`
rajan_sre: starting digest recompute: `kvadmin recompute-digests --shard 22 --fast` (this will touch primary and may create load). I recommend limiting concurrency to 1.
emma_eng: recompute started at 04:30, concurrency=1. Monitor expected to run ~12m.
infra_bot: kvadmin: recompute job submitted job=job-4521 shard=22 concurrency=1 status=running
leah_oncall: monitoring: gateway errors trending down to 0.7% at 04:38; tail latency improving. Prefetch queue drained to 6.
ops_maya: once recompute finishes, we'll allow a gradual unthrottle: restore prefetch workers to baseline slowly and close cache circuit in 10% increments with 3m observation.
rajan_sre: recompute job finished at 04:43. Post-check shows 0 inconsistent prefixes found. Scheduling shard mode back to read-write after 5m of stability.
emma_eng: re-enable writes: `kvadmin set-shard-mode 22 readwrite` — done.
infra_bot: shard 22 mode changed to readwrite.
leah_oncall: closing actions: keep cache circuit open for 10 more minutes, then step down. Also create postmortem ticket and schedule RCA meeting.
cs_paul: updated customers at 04:50; notified that mitigation complete and we are verifying for recurrence. No wg escalation requested.
ops_maya: runbook updates: add guardrail to abort compaction if digest check fails for >0.1% of prefixes, and auto-throttle prefetch when queue depth > 50.
rajan_sre: creating ticket PHAB-2027 with RCA: compaction digest drift -> eviction cascade -> prefetch storm -> gateway overload. Assigning owners: eng=emma_eng, sre=rajan_sre, ops=ops_maya.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Paging cleared at 04:52 UTC. Impact window ~34 minutes. Customer-facing impact limited to a small set of accounts; no data loss. Postmortem scheduled.
leah_oncall: handing off to rajan_sre for follow-up notes. My shift ends in 22m.
rajan_sre: taking handoff. I'll run the controlled circuit close later with checks. Tagging @cs_paul and @ops_maya for post-incident tasks.
